subject: Clarify billing minimums, context-splits, and true-up for BrightCart pilot
messages:
From: Claire Thomas <c.thomas@brightcart.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on billing units & minimums before pilot

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Before we finalize the pilot SOW, procurement has a short list of billing questions they need answered so they can sign off:

- How are billable tokens calculated for a single API call that includes a long prompt + streaming response? Do you count prompt+response (client-visible tokens) or internal framing tokens too?
- We heard mention of a minimum / quantum — what is the per-call minimum and the rounding behavior (e.g., do you round up to the nearest N tokens, and if so what N)?
- For calls that use cross-model routing (e.g., initial ingest with an embedder then generation), how are tokens attributed across SKUs?
- If we have repeated identical prefixes across sessions (customer history), is there any prefix cache crediting or is every token counted?
- For pilot true-up: does unused committed volume roll forward or is there a true-up billing at month end?

Can you send a one-pager with examples and a sample invoice line so procurement can map to our internal POs? We need this by EOW.

Appreciate it,
Claire
Claire Thomas
Head of Procurement, BrightCart
procurement@brightcart.com

Note: attaching procurement checklist separately via procurement@brightcart.com (not on this thread).
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Thomas <c.thomas@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on billing units & minimums before pilot

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together concise answers and an example invoice row below; I’ll drop a one-pager and a sample CSV after we confirm numbers. If anything below looks off, call it out and I’ll adjust.

Quick answers (high level):
1) What we bill: billable tokens = encoded input tokens (prompt + system tokens) + encoded output tokens (response). We do not charge for transport headers, but we do count model tokenization differences (so different models can tokenize a string into different token counts).

2) Rounding & minimums: we meter at a 50-token quantum by default and always round up to the nearest quantum per API request. In addition, there is a per-request floor of 100 billable tokens for streaming generation requests (this is to cover kernel warm-up and KV cache overhead). Example: a 73-token total call -> billed as 100 tokens; a 141-token call -> billed as 150 tokens.

3) Multi-model attribution: when a single logical transaction touches multiple SKUs (e.g., embedding + generation), we split the billable tokens to the SKU that executed the operation. The invoice shows separate line items by SKU and model.

4) Prefix cache / repeated prefixes: we have an optional prefix cache for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted pilots without a cache configured, repeated prefixes are billed each time. If you enable prefix caching (or reuse via session tokens), the billing engine applies a cache credit: exact matching prefix tokens are zero-rated for that call and reconciled at invoice time.

5) Pilot true-up & commitments: commitments are monthly. Unused committed units do not automatically roll forward beyond the committed month; we true-up at month end and apply any overage or credit per the SOW. For pilot concessions we can negotiate a limited roll-forward for the first 2 months (see below).

Invoice example (single line):
- Date: 2025-09-30, SKU: generation-16k, Model: rdx-gpt-16k, Quantity billed (tokens): 3,450 (billed as 3,500), Unit: tokens (50-token quantum), Unit price: $0.0006, Line total: $2.10

Next steps: can you confirm whether BrightCart will require prefix caching for production (we can include it in the pilot as an optional add-on)? Also please confirm the pilot committed monthly token amount so I can produce a sample invoice that maps to your PO number.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on billing units & minimums before pilot — pricing ask

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Claire’s procurement questions. BrightCart is green to proceed but procurement needs firm answers on rounding, minimums, and the pilot true-up. They asked for a one-pager + a sample invoice.

Proposal I’d like to offer (to get the pilot signed this week):
- Pilot: 1M committed tokens / month, 3-month pilot
- Concession: 20% on committed unit price for months 1–3
- Waive the 100-token streaming per-request floor only for the pilot (so we bill at quantum without the 100-token floor)
- Allow 1-month roll-forward on unused committed units for the pilot only

Can we approve the 20% discount and temporary waiver? If not, what’s the minimum concession we can offer without finance approval? I put the HubSpot deal HS-789201 on the note.

—Tessa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on billing units & minimums before pilot — pricing ask

Tessa — quick callouts from pricing perspective:
- 20% on committed token unit price for a 3-month pilot looks reasonable as a sales concession; acceptable to approve for deals <= $60k ARR equivalent burn in pilot. Please confirm expected spend.
- Waiving the 100-token streaming floor: acceptable as a time-limited pilot concession if we add an explicit clause that it reverts at end of pilot. Finance (Marissa) needs to confirm no accounting complications.
- 1-month roll-forward on unused committed units: this is outside standard policy but OK for pilots with defined caps; Marissa please confirm.
- We should instrument a single invoice line for committed volume and separate lines for overage SKU usage so procurement has clear mapping.

Marissa — any objections from accounting to the above? If not, I’ll signal Tessa to finalize paperwork.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales — West
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Claire Thomas <c.thomas@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on billing units & minimums before pilot — final terms and sample invoice

Claire / Tessa — redlining complete from finance. We can accept the pilot terms below:

Confirmed pilot terms (final):
- Pilot length: 3 months starting 2025-09-15
- Committed: 1,000,000 tokens / month
- Price: committed unit price $0.0006 / token, 20% concession applied months 1–3 -> $0.00048 / token for committed units
- Rounding: standard 50-token quantum; we will waive the 100-token streaming per-request floor for pilot period only (explicit revert on 2025-12-15)
- Prefix cache: BrightCart can enable prefix caching during the pilot; we will include cache credits for exact-match prefixes (documented in appendix)
- Roll-forward: unused committed units may be rolled forward for 1 month only (to the following calendar month) for pilot period
- True-up: month-end true-up will show committed line (prepaid) + overage line items by SKU/model

I attached: BrightCart_MA_plan_v1.pdf (pilot summary & T&C redline) and sample-invoice-brightcart.csv (how lines will appear).

Claire — once you confirm I’ll get countersignature instructions. Thanks for moving quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference
